name: King Island
reason: Island with Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania sources (rule 1-3): a place to go in its own right; destination-vs-spot is the proposer's call.
objection: It is a feature/area wrapper; its real draws are the spots below.

name: Naracoopa
reason: Small town named in Wikivoyage for its restaurant and cottages; nothing to do for half an hour (rule 2).
objection: A beachfront village on the east coast could be a pleasant stop, but only accommodation is cited.

name: Grassy
reason: One source, mentions only a restaurant and mine town; no sight (rule 2/3); its museum content is covered by King Island Historical Museum.
objection: Former scheelite mining town might have heritage interest.

name: Calcified Forest
reason: Great Short Walk (30 min) named by Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania: a walk to a distinct natural feature (rules 1-3).
objection: Short, and a fairly niche geological curiosity.

name: Seal Rocks
reason: Island's highest cliffs and a short walk to a lookout, start of Copperhead clifftop track; second-tier coastal stop named by Discover Tasmania. Judged on its own, not the NSW Seal Rocks.
objection: One counted source, short visit; the lookout may be a ten-minute stop.

name: Martha Lavinia Beach
reason: Surf beach named by Discover Tasmania under 'Do' (surf, beachcombing); second-tier beach (rule 1-2).
objection: One source; remote beach whose draw is mainly for surfers.

name: Sea Elephant Bay
reason: Named only for accommodation in Wikivoyage; no described activity (rule 1-2).
objection: It is a real beach at Naracoopa where one could walk.

name: Currie Lighthouse
reason: Harbour lighthouse (1879) with the boathouse and museum beside it; one source, short photo stop.
objection: For: forgiving on lighthouses, free and visible. Against: one source, exterior only, ~15 min, near-duplicate cluster with museum/Currie.

name: King Island Historical Museum
reason: Museum in the old keeper's cottage with shipwreck/sealing history and the original Cape Wickham lens, named by Discover Tasmania (rules 1-3).
objection: One source; small local museum with unconfirmed hours.

name: King Island Maritime Trail
reason: A brochure route across the island (not a place); its stops (Cataraqui, lighthouses) are judged individually (rule 3).
objection: A named, guide-promoted trail like Hump Ridge; but not walkable as one place.

name: Cataraqui
reason: Site of Australia's worst peacetime maritime disaster (1845), the Maritime Trail's headline stop; shipwreck site with memorial named by Discover Tasmania.
objection: One source; may be a memorial and a short roadside stop, and its main content is a plaque.

name: King Island Dairy
reason: Island's best-known food icon, with cheese tasting; named by Discover Tasmania.
objection: For: a headline draw people stop for, tasting counts as something to do. Against: it is a shop, not a sight (rule 2).

name: Cape Wickham Golf Links
reason: Ranked Australia's top course 2024/25, public access; a reason people fly to the island.
objection: For: a destination draw. Against: a paying golf course is a venue/activity, one source, no half-hour casual visit.

name: Ocean Dunes Golf Course
reason: Another golf course; a venue, not a sight; one source.
objection: Top-15 Australian course, public.

name: The Boathouse Restaurant With No Food
reason: A restaurant (bring your own food); a venue first (rule 2).
objection: Quirky one-off setting beside the lighthouse, a roadside-icon style stop.

name: Wild Harvest
reason: Restaurant (rule 2).
objection: Fine-dining destination named by the board.

name: King Island Distillery
reason: Distillery with tours by arrangement; not open whenever one arrives (rule 4).
objection: Tastings are a legitimate activity.

name: King Island Brewhouse
reason: Taproom venue, one source; not a sight (rule 2).
objection: Tasmania's most northerly brewery is a mild novelty.

name: Penny Royal Adventures
reason: Operator, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place).
objection: None strong.

name: Reid Rocks
reason: No counted source (re-searched: no visitor page; only Wikipedia), reserve offshore with no landing.
objection: Major fur seal colony; but no practical visitor access shown.

name: Flinders Island
reason: Island with Wikivoyage and Discover Tasmania sources; destination-level candidate, placement is the proposer's call.
objection: A wrapper for its beaches and walks.

name: Whitemark
reason: Service town; one source lists services only (rule 2).
objection: Largest town and gateway.

name: Lady Barron
reason: Ferry port with a general store; no sight (rule 2).
objection: Gateway at a low rank is allowed, but nothing to do named.

name: Killiecrankie
reason: Town is a wrapper for its own attractions (topaz hunting at Killiecrankie Bay, the Dock walk), kept separately.
objection: Two counted sources name it as a See place.

name: Killiecrankie Bay
reason: Topaz ('Killiecrankie diamonds') fossicking on the beach, a Discover Tasmania 'Don't miss' activity (rules 1-3).
objection: One source; hire of sieves is from a private operator and the town is a near-duplicate.

name: Killiecrankie to The Dock Coast Walk
reason: Coastal walk promoted by Discover Tasmania with Stackys Bight, Old Man's Head and The Dock as parts; kept as the single walk spot.
objection: One source; sub-stops are folded in here.

name: The Dock
reason: End point of the Killiecrankie walk, part of that walk (rule 3).
objection: Swimming/snorkelling is a draw of its own.

name: Old Man's Head
reason: A boulder on the same coastal walk; part of a larger spot (rule 3).
objection: Named individually in a guide.

name: Stackys Bight
reason: Sea arch on the same walk; part of the walk (rule 3).
objection: Photographed feature in the guide.

name: Strzelecki Peaks
reason: Headline summit walk, Great Short Walk, named by three counted sources including 'Don't miss'.
objection: Steep 4-5 h walk; may duplicate Strzelecki National Park.

name: Trousers Point
reason: Headline beach and Great Short Walk named by two counted sources.
objection: Inside Strzelecki National Park, so it is a near-duplicate of the park if both kept.

name: Castle Rock
reason: Great Short Walk to a named rock, second-tier walk named by Discover Tasmania.
objection: One source; limited detail.

name: Mount Killiecrankie
reason: Only listed as a possible climb with no detail (rule 1).
objection: A real summit hike.

name: Mount Boyes
reason: Only listed as a possible climb with no detail (rule 1).
objection: A real summit hike.

name: Mount Tanner
reason: Drive-up lookout with island views, one source; Walkers Lookout nearby.
objection: For: an easy view stop. Against: one source, drive-up pull-out, short.

name: Long Point
reason: No counted source (re-searched: none on Flinders Island; search matches mainland Tasmania).
objection: Tidal salt marsh on a self-guided drive.

name: Wybalenna Chapel
reason: Aboriginal exile site listed under 'Don't miss' by Discover Tasmania and Wikivoyage; chapel and cemetery accessible (rules 1-3).
objection: Small chapel, a ten-minute stop, and solemn rather than a sightseeing draw.

name: Furneaux Museum
reason: Museum at Emita named by two counted sources with distinct exhibits.
objection: Small local museum; hours limited.

name: Palana Beach
reason: White beach named by one source as the northern end of the beach run.
objection: For: second-tier beach. Against: one of 120 beaches, only a passing mention.

name: Yellow Beach
reason: White beach named by one source as the southern end of the beach run.
objection: For: second-tier beach. Against: passing mention among 120 beaches.

name: Unavale Vineyard
reason: Cellar door, a shop-like venue (rule 2).
objection: Island wine is a niche draw.

name: Furneaux Distillery
reason: Distillery with tours by appointment (rule 2/4).
objection: Peated island whisky is distinctive.

name: The Flinders Wharf
reason: Restaurant/distillery (rule 2), despite two sources.
objection: Named a 'don't miss' sunset dining spot.

name: Flinders Island Adventures
reason: Operator, not a place.
objection: Tours to offshore islands.

name: Roaring 40s Kayaking
reason: Operator, not a place.
objection: None.

name: Cape Barren Island
reason: No counted source; restricted-access community island (rules 1-2).
objection: Second-largest of the group.

name: Kent Group National Park
reason: Two Wikivoyage mentions; boat-only remote marine park with sea lions.
objection: For: wildlife and a national park. Against: boat only, no operator named, almost no visitors, access is arduous.
